timeline.title: MoU signed during US trade mission
timeline.description: Karnataka CM H.D. Deve Gowda's government signs MoU with a US-backed consortium (Kalyani Group + VHB International + SAB International) for the Bengaluru-Mysuru Infrastructure Corridor.

timeline.title: Concession Agreement with Government of Karnataka
timeline.description: BOT concession granting toll rights plus township/real-estate development rights along the corridor via BMICAPA (Bangalore Mysore Infrastructure Corridor Area Planning Authority).

timeline.title: Peripheral road sections open to traffic
timeline.description: The 41 km Peripheral Road and 9 km Link Road become operational and tolled. The flagship 111 km Bengaluru-Mysuru expressway itself is never built.

timeline.title: Lokayukta orders probe into land acquisition
timeline.description: Karnataka Lokayukta orders investigation into irregularities in land acquisition for the project, naming several former chief ministers.

timeline.title: Cost-recovery dispute drags on
timeline.description: Successive state governments review the concession; tolling continues amid disputes over what counts as recoverable 'project cost' and whether promised expressway milestones were met.

timeline.title: Only ~4 km of the expressway ever completed
timeline.description: Reported status: 4 km of expressway, 41 km peripheral road, 8.5 km link road built out of the originally envisioned corridor (Deccan Herald).

timeline.title: NHAI opens parallel Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway (NH-275)
timeline.description: The 118 km access-controlled NH-275 expressway effectively replaces the unbuilt portion of the BMIC vision; NICE tolls on the ring road continue.

analysis.summary: NICE Road remains tolled because its 1997 concession ties toll collection to recovery of a 'project cost' whose size and composition have been contested for decades - while only a fraction of the promised corridor (the ring road around Bengaluru) was ever built. The concession also bundled highly valuable real-estate development rights into the same contract, complicating any claim that tolls alone must cover costs.
reasonsStillTolled: Open-ended BOT contract: tolls run until 'full project cost + agreed return' is recovered, with no fixed end date
The 'project cost' figure has never been independently audited in public and includes disputed land and financing components
Only ~54 km (ring road + link) of the planned ~160 km corridor materialised, but the concession was never terminated or renegotiated
Real-estate/township rights (BMICAPA) were part of the concessionaire's compensation, yet tolls continue alongside them
Political inertia: every state government since 1997 has inherited the contract and litigation risk instead of cancelling it
openQuestions: What is the audited total project cost actually claimed by NICE under the concession?
How much toll revenue has NICE collected cumulatively since 2005?
What returns have lenders and shareholders already received (debt servicing, refinancing, dividends)?
What was the market value of the land transferred/acquired under the concession, and what revenue did townships generate?
What exactly does the concession agreement say about termination if expressway milestones are missed?
